english.title: Elector or proxy corruptly accept meat, drink, entertainment or provision provided to influence voting
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of a corrupt practice, in that, being

(A)_[an elector,]_
(B)_[the proxy of an elector, namely **(..SPECIFY ELECTOR..),]_

you corruptly accepted or took

(C)_[meat,]_
(D)_[drink,]_
(E)_[entertainment,]_
(F)_[provision,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THING ACCEPTED OR TAKEN..), from **(..SPECIFY PERSON FROM WHOM THING TAKEN..)

(G)_[for the purpose of corruptly influencing a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), to vote or refrain from voting]_
(H)_[for the purpose of corruptly influencing that person to vote or refrain from voting]_
(I)_[on account of a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), having voted or refrained from voting]_
(J)_[on account of that person having voted or refrained from voting]_
(K)_[on account of a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), being about to have voted or refrained from voting]_
(L)_[on account of that person being about to have voted or refrained from voting]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 114(3) and 168(1) of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being an elector or his proxy, corruptly accepted or took meat, drink, entertainment or provision
for the purpose of corruptly influencing a person to vote or refrain from voting or
on account of a person having voted or refrained from voting, or being about to vote or refrain from voting

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.
Indictment: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
